bug_semantics: An admin-issued access JWT carrying only an unrelated minimal scope such as echo:read passed JWTAuthMiddleware and reached all nine /api/panel/comments routes because those AuthRouterGroup registrations lacked RequireScopes. The comment service then checked only the database user's admin/owner role, not the access token's scopes, allowing the limited token to read comments and settings, moderate or delete comments, change comment settings, and send test email.
flaw_origin: The old comment panel routes were ordinary authenticated-admin routes before restricted access tokens existed and therefore were not independently the scope bypass. The smallest causal commit is reconstructed PR #195 member bf994ebfd5fe2e16b85ff64ad25147abd9ba99d7: it first defined comment and other scopes and changed access-token creation to accept, validate, embed, and persist selected scopes and audience while the nine comment routes remained unguarded. Its immediate parent 387667192911c86db1e1bcb3f544ce12d340ffdb could mint only the prior unscoped token. Later member b47fa1c75d890cd080e3f6699bbfca8cd8d4b939 added RequireScopes to other route families but omitted comment.go, so it continued rather than introduced the already-exploitable state.
ai_marker: The BIC Git commit object bf994ebfd5fe2e16b85ff64ad25147abd9ba99d7 has human author and committer L1nSn0w <l1nsn0w@qq.com> and the exact message line `Made-with: Cursor`; it has no bot author or AI Co-Authored-By identity.
evidence: The first-party advisory https://github.com/lin-snow/Ech0/security/advisories/GHSA-fwg7-53p4-g33c identifies the nine unguarded comment-panel routes, the limited-scope-token -> JWTAuthMiddleware -> role-only requireAdmin execution path, an echo:read-token PoC, and 4.4.3 as patched. This matches the bundle advisory's before-4.4.3 semantics.

The reconstructed PR member is not an aggregate, import, or move. The GitHub Git-commit object for bf994ebfd5fe2e16b85ff64ad25147abd9ba99d7 gives parent 387667192911c86db1e1bcb3f544ce12d340ffdb, tree 03b5c8a300d26c27fe8766e1afae1913d73849f0, and a six-file +194/-10 scoped-token schema/issuer change. Its patch adds ScopeCommentRead/Write/Mod and Scopes/Audience inputs and replaces CreateClaimsWithExpiry with CreateAccessClaimsWithExpiry. Raw comment.go at that BIC still has all nine direct AuthRouterGroup registrations without RequireScopes.

Direct-parent raw-object checks at 387667192911c86db1e1bcb3f544ce12d340ffdb show AccessTokenSettingDto contains only Name and Expiry and CreateAccessToken calls CreateClaimsWithExpiry(user, expiry), with no selectable scopes or audience. Thus the restricted credential required by the advisory cannot be minted in the immediate parent, directly establishing introducer_parent_absent=true.

The squash carrier is not used as the BIC. In the validated clone, `git show -s --format='%H %T %P' 3f8fb150158723aca31df2ae937a1aa7b31ac254` identifies aggregate tree e9484ebf85c66a09c425d8407ebfa79f57da39fa and parent 45693330c7733364027e0aa07c102c4f01aab88a; the PR #195 member chain is recorded in decomposed_shas, and bf994ebfd5fe2e16b85ff64ad25147abd9ba99d7 is the first member that creates restricted access tokens while retaining the unguarded routes.

In the validated clone, `git show -s --format='%H %P %B' 6df5673010720847e35d8bb8f60403e2cc4ab313` gives direct parent af835afe05c75bd16c7220425782ee2cd1423892. `git diff af835afe05c75bd16c7220425782ee2cd1423892 6df5673010720847e35d8bb8f60403e2cc4ab313 -- internal/router/comment.go` shows that the parent had nine unguarded registrations and the fix added middleware.RequireScopes(authModel.ScopeCommentMod) to every one, so this is the direct causal fix.

Version-boundary commands in the validated clone show `git tag --contains 3f8fb150158723aca31df2ae937a1aa7b31ac254 --sort=version:refname` begins the normal v-tag series at v4.2.1 (not v4.2.0), while `git tag --contains 6df5673010720847e35d8bb8f60403e2cc4ab313 --sort=version:refname` begins it at v4.4.3 (not v4.4.2). The repository-backed affected interval is therefore v4.2.1 through v4.4.2 and the first fixed version is v4.4.3.

The disputed verdict was rechecked against the BIC object only. GitHub's Git-commit object and raw patch header both show human author/committer L1nSn0w and the exact `Made-with: Cursor` line in bf994ebfd5fe2e16b85ff64ad25147abd9ba99d7. No PR-body marker, squash-collected message, later commit, or fix marker is used for attribution.
reasoning: Primary and reviewer agree on mechanism, decomposed smallest BIC, direct parent absence, fix, and release boundary; they disagree only between AI_CODE_FLAWED and AI_ROOT_CAUSE. The primary wins. The BIC is causally responsible for activating the bypass and its own commit object explicitly discloses Cursor assistance, so AI involvement in the flawed causal commit is established. But the same object attributes authorship and committer identity to a human and provides no bot author, AI Co-Authored-By identity, or line-level evidence that the AI itself selected or authored the security-critical omission. Treating `Made-with: Cursor` alone as proof that AI, rather than the human-authored assisted commit, was the root causal actor overstates the object evidence. AI_CODE_FLAWED captures the direct BIC-only AI signal without that unsupported stronger attribution; AI_ROOT_CAUSE is rejected.
